symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Known fixed rank of the graphon kernel.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Known bound on response levels and derivatives through order two.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Known uniform \(C^3\) radius for exposure responses.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Fixed bound for kernel size and expected-degree regularity.

symbols.name: \underline\lambda
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on nonzero graphon eigenvalues in magnitude.

symbols.name: C_{\log}
symbols.def: Fixed lower constant in the sparse-degree window.

symbols.name: b_\psi
symbols.def: Fixed moment parameter for graphon eigenfunctions.

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: Unit \(i\)'s response as a function of own treatment and treated-neighbor fraction.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Observed symmetric adjacency matrix with zero diagonal.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Generic integer degree used to define the exact lattice radius.

symbols.name: Y_i(z)
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}
symbols.def: Finite Bernoulli-policy indirect-effect estimand defined in \({\rm def:li-wager-target}\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Common localization bandwidth before exact degree adaptation.

symbols.name: \delta_N
symbols.def: Exact distance from one half to the nearest nonzero point on the degree-\(N\) exposure lattice, defined in \({\rm def:lattice-radius}\).

symbols.name: \mu_{2,i}(h)
symbols.def: Conditional binomial moment defined in \({\rm def:discrete-score}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Psi_r(A)
symbols.def: Matrix of the \(r\) eigenvectors of \(A\) with eigenvalues largest in magnitude.

symbols.name: \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
symbols.def: Nonnegative graph-observable residualization certificate returned by the PC construction.

symbols.name: \widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}
symbols.def: Nonnegative graph-observable variance remainder returned by the PC construction.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{pc}}
symbols.def: Constant \(C_{\mathrm{pc}}=2^{14}\kappa^8r^2(1+\underline\lambda^{-4})(1+B)\), fixed before observing the experiment.

symbols.name: \overline s_h(A)
symbols.def: Degree-exact standard-deviation radius defined in \({\rm def:radii}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Generic cutoff for the degree-tail testing modulus.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Generic probability law in the maintained graphon-response class.

symbols.name: \pi_{m,n}
symbols.def: For integer \(0\le m\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), the maximal expected fraction of units with realized degree at most \(m\), defined in \({\rm def:tail-modulus}\).

symbols.name: a_m
symbols.def: Largest response perturbation scale compatible with the degree-\(m\) lattice and the response envelope, defined in \({\rm def:tail-modulus}\).

symbols.name: h^\dagger
symbols.def: Smallest minimizer of the worst-case expected observable radius, defined in \({\rm def:exact-optimal-bandwidth}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak u_{n,d,L}
symbols.def: Worst-case expected graph-observable radius at \(h^\dagger\), defined in \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\).

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: Balance point \(h_0=(L^{-2}/(n\sqrt d))^{1/7}\) for \(L>0\), and \(h_0=\infty\) for \(L=0\).

standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws.

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Li--Wager known-rank \(C^3\) class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction: Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the \(r\) eigenvectors of \(A\) associated with the eigenvalues of largest magnitude; then \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\{\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top\widehat\Psi_r(A)\}^{-1}\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top\).

definitions.name: Leave-one-edge-out exact-support PC handle
definitions.construction: Start from \((I_n-\widehat\Pi_r(A))(q_{1,h},\ldots,q_{n,h})^\top\); use leave-one-edge-out eigenvector linearization before treatment weighting, retain the exact unit-specific moment equations at \(h_i(h)\), and accompany the balanced score by graph-computable residualization certificates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}\).

definitions.name: Feasible PC-balanced exact-support estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\theta_h=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\), where \(\widetilde\gamma_h\) is the score produced from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\).

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii
definitions.construction: \(\overline b_h(A)=L(6n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2+B n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\) and \(\overline s_h(A)^2=C_{\mathrm{pc}}B^2n^{-2}\{\sum_{i:N_i>0}\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}+\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\}+\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}\).

definitions.name: Same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus
definitions.construction: Let \(\pi_{m,n}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}P(N_i\le m)\). Set \(a_0=B\), \(a_m=\min\{Bm^{-1},Lm^{-2}\}\) for \(m\ge1\), and \(\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}=\max_{0\le m\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor}a_m\sqrt{\pi_{m,n}/n}\).

definitions.name: Supported and degree-exact full-class envelopes
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}=\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\}\) and \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)]\).

definitions.name: Absolute-risk and honest-length criteria
definitions.construction: \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P(\theta_n\in\mathcal C)\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]\), where the infima range over measurable procedures based on \((A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the new derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy \( |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|\le L(8n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}N_i^{-1}+Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}\). Consequently, in the degree regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6, this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\), so their Gaussian theorem is an asymptotic benchmark for \(\theta_n\), not a finite-sample same-target result.
statements.justification: The bridge states exactly when the published finite indirect effect and the finite-population derivative are asymptotically interchangeable.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition 1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets.
statements.consumer: It permits valid asymptotic comparison with Theorem 6 while keeping the proposed finite-population derivative as a distinct target.
statements.proof_tex:
Work throughout conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\).  Define the proof-intermediate function
\[
g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}{2},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), if \(N_i=m>0\), then \(M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2)\), \(Z_i\) is independent of \(M_i\), and
\[
V_i=\frac{M_i-m/2}{m}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:anonymous-interference}\), \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\), and the preceding independence, the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) is
\[
\beta_i
:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right]
=4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right].
\]
For \(m=0\), the same definition gives \(\beta_i=0\), because then \(M_i-N_i/2=0\).  Thus
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For \(m>0\), write \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^m X_j\), where the \(X_j\) are independent and take the values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\) with equal probability.  Then \(V_i\) has the same conditional law as \(S_m/m\).  Independence and centering give
\[
\mathbb E S_m^2=\frac m4,\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^3=0,\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^4
=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
+6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\,\mathbb E X_k^2
=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E V_i=0,\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^3=0,\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le \frac{3}{16m^2}.
\]
The averaging defining \(g_i\), together with \(\texttt{ass:third-derivative-bound}\), yields
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|g_i^{(3)}(x)|\le L.
\]
Taylor's formula on \([0,1]\), applicable because \(1/2+V_i\in[0,1]\), therefore gives
\[
g_i(1/2+v)
=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
\qquad |R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying by \(v\), taking the conditional expectation, and using the four displayed moments gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
&=4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],\\
|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
&\le \frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\frac{3}{16m^2}
=\frac{L}{8m}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the coefficient of \(g_i'(1/2)\) is exactly \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\), while the constant and quadratic Taylor terms vanish because \(\mathbb E V_i=\mathbb E V_i^3=0\).

By \(\texttt{def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\).  If \(N_i=0\), \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\) gives
\[
|g_i'(1/2)|
\le \frac{|\partial_x f_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_x f_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
\le B.
\]
The triangle inequality, separated over nonisolated and isolated vertices, now proves the finite-sample claim:
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|
&\le \frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
+\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
&\le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
+\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to verify the stated scale comparison.  The conditions referred to as the Li--Wager Theorem~6 regime are recorded in \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\).  In particular, there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, eventually,
\[
\rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Indeed, this follows directly from \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\).  In the same regime, conditional on \(U_i=u\), the degree is binomial with \(n-1\) trials and success probability
\[
p_n(u)=\int_0^1\min\{1,\rho_nW(u,v)\}\,dv.
\]
Because \(0<\rho_n\le1\) and \(W\ge0\),
\[
\min\{1,\rho_nW(u,v)\}\ge \rho_n\min\{1,W(u,v)\}.
\]
The uniformly positive row-integral condition in that regime therefore supplies a constant \(c_{\rm deg}>0\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
\mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]=(n-1)p_n(u)\ge c_{\rm deg}(n-1)\rho_n.
\]
For completeness, the needed lower-tail bound follows directly from exponential Markov.  If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log 2\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(S\le\mu/2)
&\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb E e^{-tS}
=e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
&\le \exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
\le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) and \((1-\log 2)/2\ge1/8\) justify the last two inequalities.  Applying this bound conditionally on each \(U_i\) and then using the union bound yields, for
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\ge \frac{c_{\rm deg}}2(n-1)\rho_n\right\},
\]
the probability bound
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{c_{\rm deg}}8(n-1)\rho_n\right\}
\longrightarrow0,
\]
because \(n\rho_n\ge n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\) there are no isolates, and the finite-sample inequality already proved implies
\[
\frac{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
\le \frac{L}{4c_{\rm deg}(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}}
\longrightarrow0,
\]
since
\[
(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}\ge (1-o(1))n^{1/4+3\varepsilon/2}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The radii \(B\) and \(L\) are fixed model-class constants, as declared in the frozen core.  Hence, for every \(\eta>0\), the event in the preceding display is eventually contained in \(\{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|/\sqrt{\rho_n}\le\eta\}\), while \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_n^c)\to0\).  This is precisely
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]
The cited theorem is centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) on the \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale.  The last display makes its centering asymptotically compatible with \(\theta_n\) at that scale, while \(\texttt{def:target}\) and \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\) remain distinct finite-sample causal functionals.  This proves the final interpretation in the proposition.

statements.statement: Over the unchanged class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), the Le Cam testing modulus generated by unsupported units and degree tails \(N_i\le m\le d/2\) is, up to constants depending only on \((B,\kappa,r,\underline\lambda)\), \(\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\). In particular, the isolated-unit component is \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\), not \(B\pi_{0,n}\). The lower experiment uses a centered two-point random-response perturbation on a least-connected latent stratum and a degree-lattice \(C^3\) bump of amplitude \(a_m\); the pairwise total variation is bounded by one quarter.
statements.justification: This separates the genuine same-class information loss from the larger safe bias allowance used by the proposed interval.
statements.gap: CaiLow2004Adaptation gives abstract modulus inequalities but not the modulus of a random graphon exposure-support tail with a realized finite-population target.
statements.consumer: It prevents an unsupported isolated-fraction upper bound from being mislabeled as a minimax lower bound and identifies the precise term a tail-adaptive estimator must attain.

statements.statement: Using \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), construct in polynomial time \(\widetilde\gamma_h(A,Z)\), \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}\), simultaneously for all \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), such that the estimator has conditional absolute bias at most \(\overline b_h(A)\), conditional variance at most \(\overline s_h(A)^2\), and the resulting interval has unconditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\). Establish \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L})\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) uniformly from \(d\asymp\log n\) through \(d=o(n)\), or determine the first larger bandwidth-dependent term forced by feasible spectral residualization.
statements.justification: The empirical-projector step is where localization can create an additional term, so the estimator and both observable PC remainders remain the first-class open construction.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph proves a global-score projector expansion in a denser polynomial-degree window; AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise does not propagate eigenvector error through exact-support causal weights.
statements.consumer: A positive or corrected answer gives a feasible bias and variance certificate for one sparse professional-network experiment.

statements.statement: Let \(h=h^\dagger\). The feasible estimator and interval produced by \({\rm oeq:uniform-feasible-pc}\) satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|\lesssim\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\ge1-\alpha\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]\lesssim\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\). The pointwise certificate is exactly \(\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)/\sqrt\alpha\), including every realized degree and isolate.
statements.justification: This is a feasible finite-sample honest upper bound whose radius never silently discards low-degree units.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is asymptotic and targets its finite indirect effect; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest has neither graph dependence nor estimated spectral balancing.
statements.consumer: Experimenters can report the realized degree certificate before deciding whether to fund an ego-cluster follow-up.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(c>0\) such that \(R^*_{n,d,L}\ge c\{\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}+\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\}\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\ge c\{\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}+\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Compatible members of the same class furnish the degree-lattice term, the interior smooth-bump term, the nonlinear honest-length term, the graph floor, and the tail modulus in \({\rm lem:tail-testing-modulus}\). No lower-bound term of order \(B\pi_{0,n}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: The converse isolates the supported-unit information frontier and the smaller genuine loss from random unsupported and low-degree units.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph leaves optimal rates open, while CaiLow2004Adaptation does not construct same-graphon response and degree-tail alternatives.
statements.consumer: The lower bound separates limitations of the Bernoulli experiment from conservatism of the proposed isolated-unit allowance.

statements.statement: Can an estimator and honest interval over the unchanged class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) replace the isolated-unit component \(B\pi_{0,n}\) inside the degree-exact upper envelope \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) by \(\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\), while retaining the exact score contribution for every \(N_i>0\)? Use cross-fitted inverse-observation imputation over estimated graphon principal-component cells as the Handle, and certify the result against the testing pairs in \({\rm lem:tail-testing-modulus}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact missing step for a full matched frontier; it is not replaced by a minimum-degree or response-sharing assumption.
statements.gap: Neither LiWager2022RandomGraph nor honest nonparametric interval theory treats latent-type-dependent missing derivative contributions from isolates in one graphon draw.
statements.consumer: Its answer determines whether the conservative interval can be shortened in the sparse logarithmic-degree regime without changing the scientific model.

statements.statement: For \(L>0\), the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\le d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\ge d^{-1/2}\). The full-class criteria obey the degree-exact sandwich \(c\{\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}+\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\}\le R^*_{n,d,L},\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\le C\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\). Whenever the low-degree increments in \(\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)\) and \(\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)\), including \(B\pi_{0,n}\), are of order \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\), the three supported-unit phases are matched; otherwise the gap between the degree-exact safe upper envelope and \(\omega^{\mathrm{tail}}_{n,d,L}\) remains open.
statements.justification: The phase diagram distinguishes the corrected supported-unit frontier from the unmatched exact low-degree and isolated-unit conservatism.
statements.gap: Existing graphon interference and honest local-polynomial results do not contain these lattice, interior, graph-floor, and degree-tail transitions.
statements.consumer: A platform can see whether more units, more connections, or tail-adaptive imputation is the relevant route to shorter intervals.

statements.statement: On the predeclared sharp-radius class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), evaluate \({\rm def:radii}\) and \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) at \(L=0\). Then \(h_0=\infty\), \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), and the positive-degree Taylor term in \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)\) is identically zero. The exact moment equation \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\) also cancels every quadratic exposure response, with affine responses as a special case. At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the nonremainder supported-unit score and graph contributions have order \(\sqrt{d/n}\), while the complete degree-exact certificate retains \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)=Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}\) and \(\overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2=C_{\mathrm{pc}}B^2n^{-2}\{\sum_{i:N_i>0}\mu_{2,i}(h_\star)^{-1}+\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\}+\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}\). An affine realized law inside \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) with \(L>0\) does not permit setting the honesty radius to zero; the reduction applies only when \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) is fixed before observing the experiment.
statements.justification: This sanity reduction shows that the exact score has no positive-degree approximation bias on the class whose third-derivative radius is fixed at zero, without hiding isolates or feasible-PC error.
statements.gap: Existing graphon-interference asymptotics do not state this degree-exact zero-remainder reduction or distinguish a predeclared zero-radius class from an affine realization inside a positive-radius honesty class.
statements.consumer: Analysts who prespecify the sharp class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) can use the largest bandwidth and report the supported-unit graph-floor certificate together with the visible isolate and feasible-PC remainders.

statements.statement: LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 assumes \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\) and \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)<0\), inherits the condition \(\inf_{u\in[0,1]}\int_0^1\min\{1,W(u,v)\}\,dv>0\), and gives a Gaussian limit on the \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale for its principal-component-balancing estimator when centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\).

source.locator: Theorem 6, equation (43), including the conditions inherited from Theorem 5

attestation.note: Verified against the arXiv v6 source at the theorem labeled theo:IND_CLT and the inherited theorem labeled theo:directCLT.

sampling_model.units: One triangular-array population with independent preassignment draws \((U_i,f_i)\); the finite-population derivative is realized after this draw.
sampling_model.network: One observed undirected graph drawn conditionally independently from the sparse finite-rank graphon \(\rho_nW\), with \(\rho_n=d/n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment is independent of the neighbor count conditional on the preassignment graph.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is known and fixed at one half; each positive realized degree uses its exact nearest nonzero exposure support, and isolates remain explicitly unsupported.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Graphon eigenfunctions are replaced by the leading empirical eigenspace; leave-one-edge-out residualization returns observable bias and variance remainder certificates.
sampling_model.inference_randomness: Coverage and risk average over the declared preassignment unit draw, graph draw, and Bernoulli assignment, as in the retained model; graph-observable radii expose the realized support contribution.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a Gaussian limit at \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale for the PC-balancing estimator centered at both the population indirect effect and the finite indirect effect under its polynomial-degree sparse regime.
Theorem 2.1 and Section 3 incorporate worst-case smoothness bias into honest fixed-length confidence intervals and bandwidth choice in nonparametric regression.
Theorems 1--3 use between-class and ordered moduli to bound expected length of honest adaptive confidence intervals.
The average direct and indirect effects decompose the derivative of Bernoulli policy value.
Theorem 2.1 supplies entrywise first-order eigenvector approximations for low-expected-rank random matrices.
Two-to-infinity expansions and rank-adaptive testing are available for possibly infinite-rank latent-position random graphs.
Approximate-neighborhood interference supports inference for causal level effects under locality conditions.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic benchmark. Proposition 1, equations (4)--(5), relates its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, and Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limit for its PC estimator in a polynomial-degree sparse regime. The present target \(\theta_n\) is a new realized finite-population derivative; \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives the exact degree-level comparison, so no finite-sample same-target tightening is claimed. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform the empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control an exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is cited only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks; the separate arXiv identifier 2504.06108 is omitted because its current contagion manuscript is not the linear-rate comparator described in the earlier core.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\). These identities do not establish the feasible spectral remainders. Isolates have no exposure variation, so the safe interval adds their full derivative envelope. Under i.i.d. preassignment responses, the corresponding same-class testing modulus is smaller, of order \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\); closing that upper--lower gap requires an estimator, not a stronger assumption.
honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is only an asymptotic benchmark after \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\). Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius; isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a proposed matching converse, and the same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus is explicit. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) upper allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. The open tail-adaptive construction must retain the i.i.d. \((U_i,f_i)\) class and the stated conditioning convention. Unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside scope.
